vedic_reference.note: Rukmini is a prominent character in Hindu mythology, particularly in the Mahabharata and the Bhagavad Purana. She is the chief queen of Krishna, who was abducted by Krishna when he was a young prince. Rukmini is considered to be an avatar of the goddess Lakshmi and is revered as a goddess in her own right.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rukmini holds significant cultural importance in Hindu society as it is the name of Lord Krishna's beloved wife and queen. In Hinduism, Krishna is considered an avatar of Vishnu, and Rukmini is revered as his devout and devoted consort. The story of their relationship is an essential part of Hindu mythology and is often depicted in art, literature, and folk songs.
data.spiritual_significance: Rukmini's name holds deep spiritual significance as she is considered a divine figure in Hinduism. Her name represents the strength and devotion of a loyal wife and the power of true love. In Hindu mythology, Rukmini is also known for her beauty, grace, and wisdom. Following the virtues of Rukmini, women in Hindu society strive to embody the qualities of a devoted and loyal partner in their marital life. Additionally, her name is a reminder of the divine union between Lord Krishna and his consort, highlighting the importance of divine love and union in spiritual growth.
